title: p0145
universal_lens: The temporal extension of a continuous production-consumption manifold introduces a partial-ordering on state vectors. The value of intermediate states is decomposed into an invariant energetic kernel and a time-dependent psychical discount factor, establishing a dualistic valuation operator across protracted dynamic systems.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the protracted production process maps to Bayesian sequential updating over latent performance states. Stored productive energy represents the posterior predictive distribution's expected value, while the direct psychical influence of time acts as a conformal discounting prior, adjusting confidence intervals for delayed consumption or realization.
gse_mapping: GSE models the division of labor as discrete state-transitions within a Markov Decision Process. Partial products are transient nodes carrying stored kinetic potential (storedup productive energy). The engine calculates optimal routing by minimizing the psychical time-discount penalty applied to future reward functions upon reaching terminal consumption states.

primitives.name: Temporal Extension Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: 130 RISK, UNCERTAINTY, AND PROFIT results are closely related to the bearings of another abstraction hitherto made, the continuity and timelessness of the production-consumption process.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: Time dimension (s), P: Production state vector (dimensionless), C: Consumption state vector (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Initial system assumes perfect knowledge and static conditions; timelessness implies instantaneous mapping from P to C.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when process latency exceeds the observational resolution, necessitating a shift from algebraic to differential topology.

layer2.mapping: Maps the timeless assumption to a zero-latency Dirac delta function in GSE state transitions. Introducing time converts this into a convolution with a delay kernel.
layer2.telemetry: Latency variance between event occurrence and data ingestion in real-time sports telemetry.

primitives.name: Partial Product Valuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Under these conditions there will be in existence at any time a complex aggregate of partial products, goods in process, which of course will have value.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: V_p: Value of partial product (Joules equivalent), A: Aggregate set of partial products (dimensionless count)
primitives.assumptions: Value is strictly positive and additive across the complex aggregate of goods in process.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if partial products exhibit negative externalities or destructive interference within the aggregate.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the Expected Value (EV) of a non-terminal game state in GSE. The 'goods in process' are the accumulated situational advantages before the final score.
layer2.telemetry: Real-time Expected Points Added (EPA) metrics tracking the value of incomplete plays.

primitives.name: Psychical Time Discount
primitives.verbatim_quote: We must separate that eleinent in the value of the partial products which is due merely to the storedup productive energy which they contain from any modification of this value due to the direct psychical influence of the time which must elapse before they are ready for consumption.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: E_s: Stored-up productive energy (J), \Delta t: Elapsed time until consumption (s), D(\Delta t): Psychical discount factor (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Value decomposition is linear and separable; psychological time preference is independent of physical energy storage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities arise when \Delta t approaches infinity or when cognitive bias causes D(\Delta t) to become hyperbolic rather than exponential.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSI's temporal decay functions applied to historical player performance data. Stored energy is the baseline skill rating; psychical discount is the recency weighting.
layer2.telemetry: Decay rate parameters in Kalman filters used for rolling performance averages.

The derivation begins by rejecting the simplification of a timeless production-consumption manifold (Quote 1). In a mathematical framework, this corresponds to moving from a static algebraic structure to a dynamic topological space parameterized by time $t$. As the process is protracted and split into complicated stages, we introduce a continuum of intermediate states, termed 'partial products' (Quote 4). These states form a complex aggregate $A$, where each element possesses an intrinsic value $V_p$. The core analytical challenge, identified in Quote 5, is the spectral decomposition of this value. We postulate that $V_p = E_s + \Psi(t)$, where $E_s$ represents the stored-up productive energy—a conserved quantity analogous to thermodynamic potential—and $\Psi(t)$ represents the modification due to the direct psychical influence of elapsed time. This duality establishes a fundamental operator in our sovereign primitives: the separation of physical capacity from temporal preference. In the context of GSI and GSE, this mirrors the distinction between a team's raw talent pool (stored energy) and the market's or coach's discounted valuation of future wins based on current delays (psychical influence). The breakdown regime occurs when the psychical discount becomes non-linear or hyperbolic, violating the separability assumption and introducing path-dependence that cannot be captured by simple scalar multiplication. Thus, the primitive operators formalize the transition from static equilibrium to dynamic, time-sensitive valuation.
